segments.name: Project Display
segments.description: Explain a scientific investigation or demonstrate a project your team has built.
segments.rules:
Bring one original project and a readable display explaining the question, method, findings and limitations. All four members should understand the work. Draft judging: scientific understanding 30%, method and evidence 30%, originality 20%, presentation 20%. Demonstrations require organiser inspection; no exposed mains wiring, open flames, hazardous chemicals, living specimens or unsupervised moving mechanisms. A safe video may replace an unsafe demonstration.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Wall Magazine
segments.description: Turn a scientific topic into an engaging wall publication.
segments.rules:
Prepare one original wall magazine on a science-related theme. Include a title, clearly organised articles or diagrams, and credits for factual and image sources. Present and explain your work individually. Draft judging: scientific accuracy 40%, communication 30%, originality 20%, presentation 10%. Use portable, non-sharp materials; confirm mounting space with organisers before preparing the final board.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Scientific Art
segments.description: Express a scientific idea through an original piece of art.
segments.rules:
Submit one original physical artwork with a short explanation of its scientific idea. Declare any assistance and credit reference material; do not enter someone else's work. Dry, safe media only. Draft judging: connection to science 40%, originality 30%, composition and technique 30%. Be ready to explain the choices behind the artwork.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Programming Contest
segments.description: Solve algorithmic problems through clear, correct code.
segments.rules:
Draft format: an individual, supervised 90-minute contest with problems in C++, Python or Java. Work independently without generative AI, messaging or internet reference material unless supplied by the organisers. Rank by problems solved, then elapsed time plus 20 minutes for each rejected submission on a subsequently solved problem; compilation errors carry no penalty. The judging environment and supported language versions will be announced before the contest.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Math Olympiad
segments.description: Explore mathematical patterns, reasoning and problem solving.
segments.rules:
Draft format: a 45-minute individual paper, with separate difficulty levels for Junior, Intermediate and Senior divisions. Show reasoning where requested. No calculators, phones or outside assistance. Rank by total marks, then marks on the designated tie-break questions; unresolved ties share rank. Organisers will publish the marking scheme before the paper begins.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Physics Olympiad
segments.description: Use scientific reasoning to explain how the physical world works.
segments.rules:
Draft format: a 45-minute individual paper adapted to each class division. Questions cover physical reasoning, everyday phenomena and age-appropriate calculations. No phones, reference materials or calculators. Rank by total marks, then designated tie-break questions; unresolved ties share rank. Required constants and the marking scheme are supplied on the paper.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Bio Chem Olympiad
segments.description: Connect biology and chemistry through observation and reasoning.
segments.rules:
Draft format: a 45-minute individual paper with division-appropriate biology and chemistry questions. This is a written contest; participants do not bring chemicals or biological specimens. No phones, notes, calculators or outside assistance. Rank by marks, then designated tie-break questions; unresolved ties share rank. The marking scheme is announced before the paper begins.

segments.name: Robot Race
segments.description: Build and guide a robot through a timed racing course.
segments.rules:
Bring one battery-powered robot per four-person team. Draft format permits remote control; one designated operator controls each run. The course is revealed before practice. Each team receives two timed attempts and its fastest completed run counts. Leaving the track requires a marshal-approved restart with a 10-second penalty. Rank by time, then fewer penalties. No damaging attachments or deliberate contact; power and size limits require organiser approval before the event.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Robot Soccer
segments.description: Combine engineering and teamwork in a robot football match.
segments.rules:
Bring one battery-powered robot per four-person team. Draft local format: one remotely controlled robot against one opponent, two three-minute halves, with a neutral ball supplied by organisers. Most goals wins; tied knockout games use a one-minute golden-goal period followed by a supervised tie-break. No trapping the ball permanently, damaging opponents or entering the field without permission. Final field and robot limits must be confirmed before construction.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Line Follower
segments.description: Program a robot to follow a marked course on its own.
segments.rules:
Bring one autonomous, battery-powered line-following robot per four-person team. After starting, remote steering is not allowed. Draft format: two timed runs; the best completed run counts. A marshal may permit up to two resets at the last checkpoint, adding 10 seconds each. Rank by time, then fewer resets. Organisers must confirm line colour, width, track surface and robot limits before final preparation.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: FIFA / EA Sports FC
segments.description: Compete head-to-head in a console football tournament.
segments.rules:
Draft format: individual console play, single-elimination matches using standard club or national teams. Six-minute halves, normal game speed, no custom teams; extra time and penalties settle draws. No pausing during active play without the opponent or referee's agreement. Report technical faults immediately; the referee decides whether to resume or replay. Exact console, game edition, controller arrangements and tournament settings remain for organiser confirmation.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Clash Royale Tournament
segments.description: Test your strategy in head-to-head Clash Royale matches.
segments.rules:
Free entry. Participants must be in the Senior division and at least 13 years old. Draft format: one-versus-one friendly battles in a best-of-three, single-elimination bracket using the agreed tournament settings. Use an eligible personal game account on a mobile device; no emulators, account sharing, automation or match-fixing. Report disconnections to the referee. This is an independently organised school tournament, not an official Supercell event.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: PUBG Mobile Tournament
segments.description: Work as a four-player squad in a tactical battle royale contest.
segments.rules:
Draft format: four-player squads in mobile-only custom rooms; no emulators, external cheats, account sharing or collaboration between squads. Three matches determine ranking. Draft placement points: 10, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 1 for first through eighth, plus one point per elimination. Ties use total wins, then elimination points, then final-match placement. Organisers confirm maps, game version, room access and device/network arrangements before play.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Valorant Tournament
segments.description: Coordinate a five-player team in a tactical PC match.
segments.rules:
Draft format: five-player teams, standard custom-game competitive settings, single-elimination best-of-one matches. Captains alternate map bans from the announced pool; the remaining map is played. Standard overtime resolves tied regulation scores. No cheats, account sharing, outside coaching during live rounds or exploiting known bugs. Referees approve technical pauses. The game version, server and PC arrangements will be confirmed before the event.

segments.name: Treasure Hunt
segments.description: Follow clues and solve challenges together around the campus.
segments.rules:
Draft format: teams of exactly three solve a sequence of science and logic clues within 45 minutes. Stay together in the marked event area; do not enter restricted rooms, move other teams' clues or interfere with participants. One hint costs two points. Rank by correctly completed checkpoints, then fewer hints, then completion time. Organisers provide the route boundaries and emergency instructions at the briefing.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Speed Cubing
segments.description: Solve a 3×3 cube with accuracy, focus and speed.
segments.rules:
Draft format: a standard 3×3×3 cube, five solves and up to 15 seconds of inspection per solve. A judge scrambles the cube and supervises timing. Remove the fastest and slowest results; average the remaining three. A missed solve is recorded as DNF under the announced judging procedure. Bring a functioning cube without electronic assistance. These local rules draw on WCA practices; this is not a WCA-sanctioned competition.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.

segments.name: Bridge Building
segments.description: Design a lightweight bridge and test its structural strength.
segments.rules:
Draft format: teams of exactly three build a bridge within 60 minutes using an identical materials kit. No pre-built parts. Organisers announce the span, load method and material allowance before the challenge. Bridges must support themselves across the gap. Rank by maximum supported load divided by bridge mass, then lower bridge mass. Testing is supervised; participants must stand clear of falling loads and follow tool-safety instructions.
Fair play: submit your own work, follow the organisers' safety instructions, and treat other participants respectfully. Raise scoring concerns with the segment lead before results are finalised. These are draft local rules and do not imply affiliation with any referenced organisation.
